title: MoST: A Foundation Model for Multi-modality Spatio-temporal Traffic Prediction

problem.claim: Spatio-temporal traffic prediction must capture complex, multi-modal, and region-specific traffic dynamics for effective cross-city deployment.

gap.claim: Existing spatio-temporal foundation models are limited to single-modal data, while multi-modality models face variable data quality and availability across cities and localized spatial patterns that hinder generalization.

contributions.claim: MoST is a foundation model for multi-modality spatio-temporal traffic prediction.
The Multi-modality Refinement Module encodes available modality data, selects task-relevant modalities, and suppresses noisy modalities.
The Spatio-Temporal Prediction Module uses multi-modality-guided spatial expert selection to identify region-specific patterns and model local dependencies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on real-world datasets.
The authors report superior performance and strong generalization capability for MoST.

narrative_sequence.summary: Accurate spatio-temporal traffic prediction supports urban traffic management and resource allocation.
Foundation models target cross-city zero-shot prediction, but existing models are single-modal and therefore limited in representing real-world traffic complexity.
Multi-modality data may provide richer context, yet data quality and availability vary across cities and spatial patterns remain highly localized.
MoST refines available modalities and uses modality-guided spatial expert selection to model local dependencies.
The authors report experiments on real-world datasets showing superior performance and strong generalization.

source_observation.claim: Available modalities can differ in quality and presence across cities, and some may contain noise.

interpretation.claim: Systems intended for cross-city transfer should adapt to missing or unreliable modalities instead of assuming a uniform input set.

application.claim: Use modality refinement and task-relevant modality selection in multi-city spatio-temporal prediction pipelines.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether adaptive modality selection is effective beyond the reported traffic-prediction setting.

source_observation.claim: Spatial patterns are localized and region-specific, limiting generalization.

interpretation.claim: Region-aware expert selection may help represent local dependencies while supporting broader transfer.

application.claim: Consider dynamically assigning spatial experts using contextual modality cues when modeling geographically heterogeneous data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which regions, datasets, or deployment conditions determine the benefit of spatial expert selection.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative performance results or baseline comparisons.
The abstract does not identify the real-world datasets, cities, modalities, or missing-data conditions used in the experiments.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, training procedure, computational cost, or zero-shot evaluation protocol.
